solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: State is holding radio prankster over cutting things

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina, a US state

indicators.note: the word 'is' holds the flipped name inside it, like a hand gripping something

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in an across clue 'over' asks for the radio name to be flipped end to end

parts.note: Jonathan Ross, who made notorious prank calls on Radio 2 in 2008

explanation.surface: A state is detaining a radio host over his cutting remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross and Russell Brand's 2008 prank phone calls on BBC Radio 2 caused the 'Sachsgate' scandal; South Carolina's postal code stands for the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Scissors are the household tool used for cutting paper or cloth, so they are literally cutting things.

clue.text: Round figure accepted by stupid prat in key part of a big company

indicators.note: to be accepted by something is to be taken inside it
the built-up group goes inside the word for the key part

parts.note: the core is the central, essential part

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so the letters of prat are jumbled

parts.note: the figure nought is round
taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: A round-figure bonus is accepted by some idiot at the heart of a big firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the idiot word is chosen so that the round figure lands in its middle; the whole group then sits inside the key part.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate is the adjective for things belonging to a large business or corporation.

clue.text: (& 22ac.) Balls' protector, mass of hair on top, who's out to wind up listeners

definitions.text: who's out to wind up listeners

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on top of the other comes first

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick, bushy mass
short for jockstrap, worn to protect the testicles

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of a sports protector topped by a wild hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: The hair piece sits on top in the down light, then the athletic support follows in 22 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock jock is a radio presenter who deliberately provokes and offends the audience to stir up controversy.

clue.text: Extension where beer belly hangs out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a part that extends over another
second reading: a paunch drooping down onto the thighs when seated

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and the second reading appears: the belly hangs over the lap.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlap is a portion that projects beyond or covers another, an extension past an edge.

clue.text: Posh, extremely shitty, concealing self-abuse?

indicators.note: the outer letters conceal the other piece by hiding it between them
extremely points at the extremes, the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word
British slang for masturbation, once primly called self-abuse

explanation.surface: Something posh turns out to be utterly shabby and hiding a solitary vice.
explanation.walkthrough: S(WANK)Y: the slang word sits inside the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Swanky is informal for stylish and expensive, a synonym for posh.

clue.text: Underwear's sexy without once being shameless

parts.note: bras are underwear; the 's makes it plural-looking

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word for once is taken out

parts.note: taken as written before cutting
ex means former or once

explanation.surface: Lingerie that is alluring without ever having been brazen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' as a former state is the crossword ex, as in ex-wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy describes someone bold and brazen, a synonym for shameless.

clue.text: Nappy contents not hot? Mind the mites

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for hot is removed from what comes before

parts.note: what fills an infant's nappy, crudely put
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warning that a nappy's contents are cold, then a reminder to watch the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H from BABY SHIT to leave BABYSIT. A nappy is a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to look after small children, the mites being little ones.

clue.text: Elastic panty hose inverted tops at "Animus"

indicators.note: something elastic stretches into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: tops are the first letters of the two words just before it

parts.note: the initial letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reads like a lingerie catalogue item, stretchy pantyhose, with a strange slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panty hose' looks like one garment, but only 'panty' goes in whole; 'hose' gives just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus means hostility or ill will, the same as antipathy.

clue.text: A bit of southern codswallop

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: A little bit of nonsense from the South.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a small piece or fragment, simply a bit.

clue.text: Cameron's main function to keep in check Clegg's core, vernacular language

indicators.note: main suggests the head, the first letter of the name

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

indicators.note: to keep something in check is to hold it in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a function is a role

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the five-letter name

explanation.surface: David Cameron's chief task in the coalition was keeping Nick Clegg in line.
explanation.walkthrough: Cameron and Clegg led the 2010 Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government.
explanation.definitionFit: A creole is a mother tongue formed from a mix of languages, a local vernacular.

clue.text: Archer extremely resentful: "time lost, judge"

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the name

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

indicators.note: lost means gone, so the letter for time drops out

parts.note: bitter means resentful
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, bitter after his time inside, rails at the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER loses one T. Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Tory peer, was jailed for perjury in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who settles disputes, a synonym for judge.

clue.text: Our feature of features doubled

parts.note: surface reading: a regular section of Private Eye, the magazine this puzzle appears in
setter's reading: faces that appear twice over, two people who resemble each other

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye runs a long-standing column pairing photos of public figures who resemble each other; 'features' means faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people with similar faces are each other's double, and the magazine's column is named for them.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) Seed expelled initially by penis, which gets the hymn-singers going?

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter
a familiar euphemism for the male member

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of seed being ejaculated, which then switches to a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The bawdy reading of 'seed' and 'organ' is the cover; the definition is innocent church music.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe organ accompanies hymns in church, so it leads the congregation into song.

clue.text: They stand by bets, swallowing hard

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
up as in erect, the setter's smutty sense of hard

explanation.surface: Gamblers' wagers that make someone gulp hard.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK(UP)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Backups are reserves kept ready to replace something that fails, things that stand by.

clue.text: Worn out having a ball or two?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for utterly exhausted
second, jokey meaning: equipped with testicles, which British slang calls knackers

explanation.walkthrough: British slang calls the testicles knackers, so the word for exhausted can be read as 'equipped with balls'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is everyday British slang for exhausted, tired out completely.

clue.text: see 28ac.
Live comics about to go off atrocious leader

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so what is left is spoiled into a new order
to go means to leave, so the letter for about is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Stand-up comedians about to perform a set mocking a brutal dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Cs goes; the other nine letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Slobodan Milosevic was the Serbian president tried for war crimes, a notoriously brutal head of state.

clue.text: Dave's top "expert", arse-over-tip politician with singular flies

indicators.note: top is the first letter of the name

parts.note: the first letter of the name

indicators.note: falling head over heels turns something upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ace is an expert
Member of Parliament
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: David Cameron's so-called top expert falls over, a politician with his trouser flies open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like the trouser zip; it is the verb, the definition. Arse-over-tip is British slang for head over heels.
explanation.definitionFit: Decamps means leaves suddenly or runs off, which is a sense of flies as a verb.

clue.text: Smoker with yen for dodgy advertising

parts.note: someone who puffs on a cigarette
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A smoker craving cigarette advertising of a shady kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like a craving; it is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffery is exaggerated, overblown praise used in promotion, so hype of a dubious sort.

clue.text: Brenda overturned by revolution — don't waste it!

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose royal cipher is ER
a revolution is one turn of a cycle

explanation.surface: The Queen toppled by a revolution, with a green slogan tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle something is to reuse it rather than throw it away, the opposite of wasting it.

clue.text: Conservative Neal's outburst (very English): "Country surrounded by bloody foreigners"!

indicators.note: an outburst blows things apart, so these letters scatter and reform

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's very English rant about a nation hemmed in by foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bloody foreigners' turns a neutral definition into a jingoistic quote.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory wholly enclosed within another state, so foreign land on every side.

clue.text: Sun's far right wing boss with elevated beer belly?

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevated means raised, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a pot belly

explanation.surface: The Sun's hard-right editor, sporting a raised paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Sun's', meaning 'the Sun is': a red-top. The Sun is a British tabloid, and tabloids are called red-tops after their red mastheads.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-top is a British downmarket tabloid, and the Sun is the best-known example.

clue.text: (see 3dn.)
see 12ac.
Nick's fresh balls-up which has tongues wagging

indicators.note: a balls-up is a mess, so these letters end up muddled

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg's latest blunder sets everyone gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongues wagging' looks like gossip, but here the tongues are literally busy.
explanation.definitionFit: A French kiss is an open-mouthed kiss using the tongue, so tongues really are moving.

clue.text: Price of the ultimate in shit in IKEA — horrendous?

indicators.note: horrendous suggests a hideous mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the ultimate is the last, so only the final letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking what flat-pack junk at IKEA really costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price' looks like cost; it is a surname. Katie Price is a British glamour model and reality-TV celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the first name of Katie Price, so it completes the surname given.

clue.text: General habit of bloke: squeezing member

indicators.note: squeezing grips something tightly inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a gent is a man, a bloke
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A man's routine of gripping his member, with a smutty hint.
explanation.walkthrough: G(ARM)ENT. 'General' looks like an army officer to abbreviate to G, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is an item of clothing such as a nun's robe, and garment is the general term for any such item.

clue.text: "Performing" Bill approved? Cyclops has

parts.note: a parliamentary bill that has been passed becomes an Act
the setter saying 'I have', contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Asking whether a performing bill got the nod, with the setter claiming one.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter refers to himself by his pseudonym, so 'Cyclops has' is 'I've'.
explanation.definitionFit: Active means busy or in operation, so a performing machine or person is active.

clue.text: (&15ac.) How to get through a dry period by avoiding seeing two or more ex-political broadcasters together?

definitions.text: How to get through a dry period by avoiding seeing two or more ex-political broadcasters together?

parts.words: How to get through a dry period
parts.note: surface reading: the slogan of staying sober, taken step by step

parts.words: avoiding seeing two or more ex-political broadcasters together
parts.note: setter's reading: never letting more than a single Sir Robin Day appear at once

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robin Day was a famous BBC political interviewer; the setter imagines a world with several of him, to be met singly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the Alcoholics Anonymous motto for staying off drink, taking each sober day as it comes.

clue.text: Posturing after tax returns concealed by crooked creep

indicators.note: to be concealed by is to be hidden inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: first part of the rearranged word

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so this word is read backwards
something crooked is bent out of shape, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: net pay is pay after tax
remaining part of the rearranged word

explanation.surface: A slimy creep is caught posing after fiddling his tax returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax returns' looks like a form to file; 'after tax' is take-home pay and 'returns' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretence is a false show or affectation, the same as posturing.
